title: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion
claim: A reconstructed 4D scene scaffold lets one input video be re-rendered consistently along several different camera paths.
layout: 2 side-by-side examples, each stacked top-to-bottom: input, 3D reconstruction, outputs
description: The figure shows two examples side by side, each with the same three-row structure. The top row is a strip of three input video frames with colored 3D trajectory traces overlaid, labeled "Input" in red. The middle row is a 3D point-cloud reconstruction of the scene, with colorful trajectory streaks on the moving subject. A red camera frustum marks the source view and blue frustums mark target views, each labeled with its camera path (Left arc, Face arc, Crane above, Arc left-right). The bottom rows give three generated frames for each target path, labeled vertically, and the projected trajectories are overlaid on the middle frame. The left example is a man by a teal car. The right example is a woman walking past columns. The eye goes first to the point clouds with their camera frustums.
caption: 4D reconstruction as a scaffold for video reshooting. Top: input video with its 3D trajectories (projected onto the image plane for visualization). Middle: reconstruction with the source camera (red) and target cameras (blue) for camera paths from Vista4D’s benchmark. Bottom: HOLO4D outputs for each path; the middle frame overlays the projected trajectories (subset shown).
abstract: Synthesizing a monocular video from a new camera trajectory requires preserving the observed scene geometry and motion while completing regions that become newly visible. Feed-forward 4D reconstructors recover the structure of the observed scene, whereas video diffusion models provide a generative prior for completing unseen content. We introduce Holo4D, a video reshooting framework that uses reconstructed 3D trajectories as a holistic source-view 4D scaffold. We project these trajectories into the requested views and encode their geometry and source appearance to guide a pretrained video diffusion model. Together with the source video and target cameras, the scaffold grounds generation in reconstructed observations while leaving unsupported regions to the generative prior. Experiments demonstrate the value of trajectory-based conditioning for camera control and novel-view synthesis. The framework accommodates different 4D reconstructors without retraining the video generator, allowing it to benefit from future advances in source reconstruction. More details can be found in our project page.
